comparisons.peer_topic: Impact of Pillar Two on company's 2024 financials
comparisons.peer_summary: The impact of Pillar Two legislation on the company for the fiscal year 2024 was immaterial, and the company continues to evaluate the impact of proposed and enacted legislative changes on its effective tax rate and cash flows as new guidance becomes available.
comparisons.comparison: Both QCOM and AMD explicitly disclose that the impact of OECD Pillar Two legislation on their 2024 financial results was immaterial. QCOM states it does not currently expect a material impact on consolidated financial statements, while AMD confirms the impact was immaterial and notes it continues to evaluate changes to its effective tax rate and cash flows.

sentences.text: While we do not currently expect this to materially impact our consolidated financial statements, we continue to monitor the impact as countries implement legislation and the OECD provides additional guidance.
For 2024, the impact to us associated with Pillar Two was immaterial.
We continue to evaluate the impact of proposed and enacted legislative changes to our effective tax rate and cash flows as new guidance becomes available.

peer_results.rationale: The submitted candidates for Broadcom are either generic statements about omitted schedules (avgo_2024_15_D001) or general critical accounting policies regarding estimates (avgo_2024_7_D032) that do not specifically address OECD Pillar Two or global minimum tax implementation status/impact.

While Intel mentions Pillar Two as one of many factors impacting its effective tax rate (intc_2024_7_D152), it does not provide specific disclosure on the implementation timeline or the actual financial impact (material vs. immaterial) for the company in 2024/2025 comparable to the specific findings reported by QCOM, AMD, NVDA, and MU. The other candidate (intc_2024_7_D008) is unrelated to tax policy.

comparisons.peer_topic: OECD Pillar Two Tax Legislation Impact
comparisons.peer_summary: The OECD Pillar Two legislation is effective for the company in 2025 and is expected not to materially impact the 2025 effective tax rate. However, other countries including Singapore plan to adopt similar legislation effective in 2026, which would significantly increase tax expense.
comparisons.comparison: Both QCOM and Micron disclose that OECD Pillar Two legislation will become effective for them in fiscal year 2025 and that they do not expect a material impact on their 2025 effective tax rate. Both companies also state they are monitoring the implementation of legislation and OECD guidance, though Micron additionally highlights that future enactments in other jurisdictions (like Singapore in 2026) could significantly increase tax expense, a nuance not present in QCOM's current disclosure.

sentences.text: Certain countries have implemented or are in the process of implementing the Pillar Two legislation, which will apply to us beginning in fiscal year 2025.

While we do not currently expect this to materially impact our consolidated financial statements, we continue to monitor the impact as countries implement legislation and the OECD provides additional guidance.
The OECD has announced a framework to implement a global minimum tax of 15% (referred to as Pillar Two).

Further changes in the tax laws of foreign jurisdictions could arise as a result of the base erosion and profit shifting project, including Pillar Two Model Rules ("Pillar Two"), undertaken by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development ("OECD").
Nearly all European Union member states have enacted the Pillar Two legislation, which will be effective for us in 2025.

While we do not expect these enacted laws to materially impact our effective tax rate for 2025, additional countries where we operate, including Singapore, have announced plans to adopt Pillar Two legislation.
Enactment of this legislation would become effective for us in 2026 and significantly increase our tax expense.
